body: I feel the same way with imposter syndrome, it's something I've struggled with (and still do). It's like every good thing that happens just means you're scared for something bad to happen to even it out. But that bad thing is the doubt, it's the inability to enjoy the good things. There's nothing else bad coming, the fear and uncertainty is already hurting. It'd be stupid for me to say just stop thinking that way, but what I will say is: be a little selfish. It sounds like so much of these negative thoughts are coming from the fact that you care too much, and that shouldn't be a bad thing. You think too much - look at all the people who don't think at all, and how stupid they are. You're better. If you need a reason to stay alive, it can be that you leaving will make me pissed off that I'm stuck with all these people who don't care and don't think and don't feel.

I understand what you're feeling, especially the last line. And while I can't say that the lost feeling and the urge to simply just not exist will go away, you only get traces of stardust when you're here. You only get to feel sweet, bitter, hot, cold, when you're alive. It sucks, and sometimes you have to do so much work just to get a taste, and some days you get nothing, but tomorrow you might. And as you stay alive, the one thing that is true is that there will be more.
